# Original Unit3 practice —50marks
Suggested40minutes writing; formative classroom sample, not official examination format. Eight short tasks32marks + two extended18marks. Use the stimulus; show working.

## S1 (4 marks)
Trace the stock code in the stimulus. Give both final dictionaries (2) and explain why the snapshot is unchanged (2).

## S2 (4 marks)
Records A03:2,A01:1,A02:2 are insertion-sorted stably by quantity. Give final ID order (2), explain equal-key order (1) and justify whether ID binary search is valid directly (1).

## S3 (4 marks)
A binary-search loop uses low < high with inclusive endpoints. Identify the boundary repair (1); give a smallest revealing test and expected result (2); state the sorted-key precondition (1).

## S4 (4 marks)
Explain an overridden label() in Camera and Projector subclasses (2), a polymorphic call (1) and a repeated-return stock test (1).

## S5 (4 marks)
For192.168.80.34/27 give mask, network, broadcast and ordinary capacity (1 each).

## S6 (4 marks)
For a remote server with no NAT, explain remote IP destination and local next-hop MAC (2). Compare TCP reliability with UDP and state an encryption caveat (2).

## S7 (4 marks)
15clients need8Mbit/s each over100Mbit/s: demand and bottleneck (2).300MB at100Mbit/s: ideal time (1) and one limitation (1).

## S8 (4 marks)
Explain why routed VLANs alone do not enforce a guest restriction (2). Interpret unanswered middle traceroute probes followed by a responding destination (2).

## E1 (8 marks)
Design available_ids(records): return the unique IDs with quantity>0, in input order, without modifying records. Records are valid (unique string ID,non-negative integer quantity) pairs. Write code/pseudocode (4); give empty,zero and mixed tests with expected outputs (3); explain dictionary versus list choice for repeated ID lookup (1).

## E2 (10 marks)
Allocate192.168.90.0/24 to Studio45endpoints+gateway, Staff20+gateway, Devices9+gateway, Guests5+gateway. Give each smallest ordinary LAN prefix (4); aligned nonoverlapping allocation (2); one correct gateway per group (2); explain where guest restriction is enforced (1); identify a required narrow service dependency (1).
